articles.title: India's Push for Global South Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Framework
articles.summary: India advocates for a unified global governance model for Digital Public Infrastructure to enhance financial inclusion across developing nations.
prelims: DPI encompasses foundational digital layers: Identity (Aadhaar), Payments (UPI), and Data Exchange (Account Aggregator).
Global South DPI initiatives focus on open-source, interoperable technology transfers.
The G20 Framework on DPI serves as the baseline for international adoption and standardized digital architecture.
articles.mains: Evaluates the role of soft-power diplomacy through technological export in strengthening India's leadership in the Global South.

articles.title: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS): Framework for Compliance Market
articles.summary: The Ministry of Power details operational guidelines for the compliance carbon market under the Energy Conservation Act.
prelims: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) acts as the administrator for the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
Designated entities receive annual Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission intensity targets.
Non-compliant entities must purchase Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) to meet their statutory obligations.
articles.mains: Analyze how a functional domestic carbon market balances industrial growth with India's Net-Zero 2070 climate commitments.

articles.title: NISAR Earth Observation Satellite: Dual-Frequency Radar Applications
articles.summary: Joint ISRO-NASA mission NISAR delivers high-resolution imagery for monitoring ecosystem changes and natural hazards.
prelims: NISAR utilizes dual-frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar: L-band (NASA) and S-band (ISRO).
It provides global coverage every 12 days to monitor land surface change, crustal deformation, and ice sheet dynamics.
Operates in a sun-synchronous orbit, delivering all-weather, day-and-night imaging capabilities.
articles.mains: Highlight the significance of international space collaborations in enhancing disaster risk reduction and climate monitoring.

articles.title: PM-JANMAN Scheme: Welfare Delivery for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
articles.summary: Progress review on critical infrastructure delivery across 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
prelims: PVTGs are characterized by stagnant/declining population, pre-agricultural technology, extreme poverty, and low literacy.
Dhebar Commission (1973) created Primitive Tribal Groups as a distinct category, renamed PVTGs in 2006.
PM-JANMAN integrates 11 critical interventions across 9 central ministries to address basic amenities.
articles.mains: Discuss the structural challenges in executing targeted welfare schemes for geographically isolated indigenous populations.

articles.title: Sub-Categorization of Scheduled Castes: Operational Framework for States
articles.summary: States initiate empirical data collection following Supreme Court guidelines on sub-classification within reserved categories.
prelims: Seven-judge Supreme Court bench affirmed sub-categorization within SC/ST categories under Article 341 and 342.
Sub-categorization mandates quantifiable and empirical data showing inadequate representation of specific sub-groups.
The judgment laid down that sub-classification cannot result in 100% reservation for any single sub-group.
articles.mains: Critically examine the implications of sub-categorization of Scheduled Castes on social equity and affirmative action policies in India.
